name: Accordion

a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-05-26 — production behavior verified in Storybook; argTypes and required stories aligned with validate:components.

forbiddenUse: put primary navigation inside an accordion. AT users land on
nest accordions more than one level deep. Two-level
ship long, scrollable panels. If the content scrolls inside
dense: Exclusive disclosure group: items {id,title,content}, one open at a time (click open item to close), optional defaultOpenId; trigger button wires aria-expanded/aria-controls to its region

usage.description: Accordion is the exclusive disclosure group: pass `items` ({id, title, content}) and at most one stays open — opening another closes the previous, clicking the open one closes it. Use it for FAQs and reference content where users need one answer at a time. For a single independent "show more" use ExpandableSection; if most readers need all the content, use plain headings instead of hiding it.

bestPractices.description: Use it for scannable reference content (FAQs, specs) where one section at a time is the point.
Keep titles short questions or labels; the trigger is a button, not a heading replacement.
Set defaultOpenId to the question most visitors came for.
Keep ids stable — they key the open state and the trigger/region ARIA pairing.
Do not hide task-critical content in an accordion; required steps must be visible by default.
Do not use it when users need to compare sections side by side — exclusive open forbids that; use headings.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: One id-keyed entry; open state derives from the id match.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: Button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, keyboard operable, chevron reflects state.

anatomy.name: Region
anatomy.description: The revealed content panel labelled by its trigger.
